title: Heatmap Pass 3 — External Research

headline_finding.title: Own-market calibration shape conflict
headline_finding.detail: Project's instr_v8 (2026-09-10) found slope falling ~1.29->~1.14 with horizon; primary external source arXiv:2602.19520 finds slope rising 0.99->1.32 pooled, and a noisy but net-rising Politics-specific pattern (1.34->1.73). Both agree on direction (underconfidence) but disagree on shape. Not fully explained by population, weighting, or anchoring differences alone.
headline_finding.reason: Pass 2's register has no entry for this specific test (instr_v8 produced a live, non-closed finding, not a CLOSED-STRONG ruling) - flagged with equivalent seriousness per instruction regardless.

findings.question: Has VPIN (volume-synchronized probability of informed trading) been applied to prediction markets?

source.title: Per-Market Information Leakage and Order-Flow Skill

findings.effect_size: Ground-truth VPIN positively predicts Brier scores (forecast accuracy); Gibbs spread negatively predicts them. Inferred VPIN diverges substantially from ground-truth VPIN; OFI estimates directionally biased.

additional_source.title: classical VPIN critique
additional_source.note: VPIN's predictive power for volatility is a mechanical artifact of trade-classification error under Bulk Volume Classification, not fundamentals-based - pre-existing methodological warning for inferred VPIN.

findings.cheap_win: partial - ground-truth-vs-inferred distinction is load-bearing, needs design work, not a drop-in replication

findings.question: Is there published work on detecting information leakage in prediction markets?

source.title: ForesightFlow: An Information Leakage Score Framework for Prediction Markets

companion_sources: arXiv:2605.02286 (Empirical Evaluation of Deadline-Resolved Information Leakage)
findings.effect_size: Skilled accounts + market makers (<3.5% of accounts) capture >30% of platform gains (from companion paper 2605.02287)
findings.cheap_win: yes - unambiguously, a maintained framework with public code already exists under the same name/concept

findings.question: Is bet/position sizing established as predictive of trader skill anywhere?

source.title: Application of the Kelly Criterion to Prediction Markets

findings.effect_size: Theoretical: misjudged position sizing degrades portfolio growth rate via KL-divergence between belief and true distribution - position size QUALITY not raw size is the signal.
findings.consistency_with_project: Consistent with project's own null finding on kelly_alignment_score (built_b5, found null/negligible under Stage 0b)
secondary_sources: Polyburg blog (flagged secondary): bet size is a wallet-relative, track-record-filtered confidence signal, not absolute-dollar

Mitts & Ofir 2026 (SSRN 6426778): bet size used jointly with timing/profitability/concentration in a composite insider-detection score, 93000 markets/50000 wallets, ~$143M flagged - position size never used in isolation
findings.cheap_win: no - position size alone is not established as an isolated predictive signal anywhere found

findings.question: Does published work find trader/forecaster skill is category-specific?

source.note: General forecasting research (Tetlock, foundational): domain expertise is NOT a reliable predictor of forecasting skill - cognitive style dominates.

conflicting_source.title: Decomposing Crowd Wisdom: Domain-Specific Calibration Dynamics in Prediction Markets
conflicting_source.note: Directly studies domain-specific calibration dynamics but category-specific slope numbers not fully extractable this pass (PDF compression-encoded).

secondary_sources: Prediction-market-specific trading blogs claim category specialization IS load-bearing with non-transferable skill profiles - not peer-reviewed
findings.verdict_detail: Genuinely contested in the literature, not cleanly answered either way

findings.question: Correlated positions across markets as a skill/informedness signal
findings.searched: Trader-level cross-market position correlation as an informedness signal - specifically distinguished from market-level price-consistency arbitrage

adjacent_found.title: Executable Arbitrage and Market Efficiency in Prediction Markets

findings.note: These are about market-level price-consistency arbitrage, not trader-level correlated position-taking as a skill signal - different question, no paper found on the actual RQ.

findings.question: Multivariate Kelly criterion for correlated positions

source.title: Efficient Multivariate Kelly Optimization Reveals Sigmoidal Scaling Laws

findings.effect_size: Reduces naive O(2^N) multivariate Kelly optimization to O(N) via integral-transform method, tractable for hundreds of simultaneous correlated bets.
findings.note: General portfolio-optimization result, not validated as a prediction-market trader-SKILL-DETECTION tool - answers how an optimal bettor would size, not whether observed sizing reveals skill.

findings.question: Does crowd vs elite/sophisticated-trader divergence predict outcomes?

source.title: Prediction Market Accuracy: Crowd Wisdom or Informed Minority?

findings.effect_size: ~3.14% of accounts (sign-randomization test, 1.72M accounts, 210322 markets, $13.76B volume) are a persistently-skilled informed minority; crowd generates most volume, little information, its losses fund the minority's profits.
findings.cheap_win: YES - the single clearest case in Job A: project's own RQ3.2 sat ABANDONED-UNTESTED while the exact paper needed to answer it was already being used elsewhere in the project (for the directional-skill persistence benchmark) and nobody closed the loop back to RQ3.2 itself.

findings.question: Signal credibility index validation

source.title: The Signal Credibility Index for Prediction Markets: A Microstructure-Grounded Diagnostic with Weighted and Time-Varying Extensions

findings.effect_size: Persistence-ratio component on logit prices, weighted Cobb-Douglas form with flow-concentration HHI, time-varying real-time spec, Monte Carlo validation incl. OOD stress tests and coordinated multi-wallet manipulation scenarios.
findings.caveat: Paper's own tau*=0.27 threshold calibrated to its own simulation universe - 'empirical applications should recalibrate by domain, platform, and response horizon' - not a universal drop-in.
findings.cheap_win: strong - project's own signal_credibility.py (built_b10-equivalent, live per pass-1 correction but annotation-only, never graduated past its 20-market gate) has less validation depth than this published version.

findings.question: How does human-level relevance-classification recall compare across similar NLP tasks?

source.note: Comparable relevance/frame-classification benchmarks report F1 0.94-0.98 (DeBERTa 0.98, Claude zero-shot 0.96, Llama3-70B 94.4% fake-news F1) - above project's 90.35% recall. But a media-bias benchmark reports F1 as low as 0.381 - task difficulty range is enormous and domain-dependent.

findings.conclusion: Does not contradict the project's own diagnosed conclusion (diffuse, 18-subtype failure) - no benchmark studied this exact task.

findings.searched: Academic methodology for LP/market-maker exclusion in prediction-market aggregate positioning strategies
findings.found: Only generic 'smart money concept' trading-blog material (not academic) and general market-microstructure literature on LP/taker clustering by order-flow pattern (not skill).

project_finding.description: Logistic recalibration slope >1 at every lead time, FALLING ~1.29 (near resolution) -> ~1.14 (weeks out). Geo/Elections only, price-weighted, tape_end-anchored, 9739 markets.

external_finding.title: Decomposing Crowd Wisdom: Domain-Specific Calibration Dynamics in Prediction Markets
external_finding.population: 353M trades, 429000 binary contracts, Kalshi+Polymarket, all 6 categories
external_finding.polymarket_specific: pattern visible across three comparable domains, blended mean slope 1.45 for political markets excluding two shortest horizons - full breakdown not extractable this pass
external_finding.anchor: close_time - trade_time, conceptually similar to but not identical to tape_end

findings.explained_by: Not fully explained. Two of three candidate explanations present but unconfirmed sufficient: (a) population breadth (narrow Geo/Elec vs broad Politics+Kalshi+Polymarket pooled), (b) weighting scheme (price vs position-size weighted - paper notes larger positions associate with prices further from truth, suggesting this could matter), (c) anchoring plausibly NOT the driver since both use trade/close-based anchors not raw resolution_date.

project_finding.description: 37.0% BH-adjusted persistence, CI [0.2945,0.4521], 146-trader cohort vs 18.6% comparison; temporal split at T_split

external_finding.title: Prediction Market Accuracy: Crowd Wisdom or Informed Minority?
external_finding.method: split-half by randomly dividing each trader's own events in half
external_finding.result: 44% of traders classified skilled on first half also classified skilled on second half; ~3% of accounts classified skilled overall

findings.explanation: Confirmed methodological difference: temporal split (project) vs random split-half (external). Population difference: narrow Geo/Elections PIT-legal vs all-category Polymarket. No numerical conflict - project's CI [29.45%,45.21%] contains 44% - but cannot be read as a replication given the split-methodology difference.

findings.topic: Copy-trade decay vs published price-discovery speed

project_finding.description: COLLAPSES-BEFORE-CADENCE, no CI-excludes-zero edge at/beyond N=15min, +0.01233 CI[-0.00186,+0.02410] at N=15min

external_finding.title: When Do Markets Fully Process Public Information? Evidence from Real-Time Prediction Markets
external_finding.result: 1-minute change in benchmark probability model associated with only 0.64-for-1 contemporaneous price change; missing 0.36 predicts drift over 'following several minutes', underreaction larger in low-liquidity markets

findings.explanation: External paper measures market-wide reaction to PUBLIC news signals; project's question is about copying an INDIVIDUAL informed trader's position - different mechanism. A 'several minutes' underreaction window is not inconsistent with nothing capturable remaining by 15 minutes. No paper found reporting a quantified copyable-window edge magnitude comparable to project's cost floors - search came back empty.

findings.topic: Falsified-selectors pattern (naive selection fails to beat matched control)

project_finding.description: Repeated pattern: non-selected/placebo/comparison group matches or beats a selected skilled group

external_finding.title: Who Profits from Prediction Markets? Execution, not Information
external_finding.result: Retail traders pick winners 51.3% of the time yet LOSE money; automated traders are coinflip-accurate (50%) yet earn $133M; directional and execution skill nearly orthogonal, shared variance <1% for humans (replicates in CBOE equity options, though the accuracy-profitability inversion does not replicate there)

findings.explanation: Strong independent support for the project's working explanation (execution not information drives profit) of WHY naive skill-selection fails to beat matched controls. No other paper found reporting the specific empirical PATTERN itself in prediction markets or sports betting - two targeted searches came back empty.

findings.topic: is_taker structural explanation (zero maker rows database-wide)

project_finding.description: Hypothesis: CLOB taker's wallet sends the settling transaction; resting maker order may never generate its own transaction hash

external_finding.note: Polymarket's matching is off-chain (operator), settlement on-chain via Polygon; relayer infrastructure batches and pays on-chain cost so users don't submit a transaction per fill.

findings.explanation: Relayer/gas-abstraction detail is not a clean confirmation of the project's specific hypothesis - if a relayer batches and submits on behalf of both sides, the simple taker-sends-it story is at least incomplete. The real explanation for zero-maker-detection may lie in transaction-hash attribution within relayer batches, not a maker/taker on-chain asymmetry per se. Flagged, not resolved - no primary source reachable (official docs silent on this point, Medium deep-dive 403'd).

findings.finding: UMA optimistic-oracle vote concentration: top 10 wallets cast >50% of dispute votes; ~60% of active UMA voters linkable to Polymarket trading accounts; ~1 in 5 disputes had a voter with an open position in the judged market; 1150+ disputed markets in 2026 already exceeding full-year 2025, ~$5B at stake across ~2000 contracts. Baseline dispute rate ~1.5% of proposals.

findings.finding: Wallet-level composite informed-trading screen using bet size + timing + profitability + directional concentration jointly, applied to 210000+ wallet-market pairs, 93000+ markets. 69.9% win rate on flagged trades, >60 SD above null under permutation test, ~$143M aggregate anomalous profit.
